## 1. Why Quarto?

Quarto is the next-generation scientific reporting engine that eliminates error-prone copy-pasting by unifying **narrative prose**, **$LaTeX$ mathematics**, and **executable analytical code** into a single source of truth.

---

## 2. Mathematical Typesetting (LaTeX)

Inline mathematical equations are written using single dollar signs: the sample observation is $y_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$.

Displayed block equations use double dollar signs:

$$
y_{ij} = \mu + \tau_j + \epsilon_{ij}, \quad \text{where} \quad \epsilon_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)
$$

The Closed-Form Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimator is:

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = (\mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{X})^{-1} \mathbf{X}^T \mathbf{y}
$$

---

## 3. Sourcing R Scripts & Loading Pre-Generated Figures

We can source our decoupled R script to run the pipeline and embed the pre-rendered plot.

```{r}
#| label: source-pipeline
#| include: false
# 'include: false' runs the script silently in the background
source(here::here("R", "01_project_discipline.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reaction-latency
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of response latencies across experimental arms."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "75%"
#| echo: false

knitr::include_graphics("output/reaction_plot.png")
```
